A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same noise-enhanced hallucination-detection study. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–I are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original hallucination-detection experiments across GSM8K, CSQA, and TriviaQA, including model comparisons, ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments, including detection AUROC, generation accuracy, uncertainty estimates, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same uniform activation noise, shared noise across selected layers, temperature-based token sampling, and uncertainty scoring. The new Figure 2 illustrates this existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same mathematical reasoning, commonsense multiple-choice, and factual question-answering coverage using GSM8K, CSQA, and TriviaQA. No additional dataset or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same participants: no-noise sampling; Predictive Entropy, Lexical Similarity, Semantic Entropy, EigenScore, and selfCheckGPT-NLI in Table 4; input perturbations in Table 7; and dropout in Appendix E.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, six evaluated models, answer processing, AUROC and accuracy metrics, sample counts, temperatures, and perturbation settings remain unchanged. The rearranged displays introduce no new evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Both retain the same analyses of sample count, uncertainty metric, temperature, noise magnitude, layer selection, and input perturbation. Appendices retain the Gaussian, attention, dropout, calibration, Pareto, zero-mean, and shared-versus-independent-noise analyses.

E5.justification: Both report 25 bootstrap resamples from 40 generated samples, with means and 95% confidence intervals for the main comparison and sample-count analysis. No run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical results and plotted data match, including Appendix A.3. For example, Table 3 retains GSM8K AUROC 76.53 without noise and 82.70 with noise for Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct. The reformatted sample-count figure preserves its curves and confidence bands.

T1.justification: The Bayesian formulation, surrogate distribution, answer-entropy definition, and Appendix B assumptions and weight-to-bias perturbation derivation are unchanged. No formal result or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions retain the same training-free Bayesian perturbation approach and claims of improved detection across datasets, models, and uncertainty metrics. The added conclusion fragment introduces no distinct contribution.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning complementary uncertainties, perturbation robustness, reasoning-chain effects, TriviaQA saturation, and dropout limitations are retained. The new illustration restates the existing mechanism without adding substantive qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same prompts, answer extraction, model-specific layer ranges, noise selections, pyvene implementation, A100 hardware, and latency statement. Technical and resource-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and Section 5 positioning relative to Bayesian networks, uncertainty metrics, single-inference detectors, and input perturbations are unchanged. The new acknowledgment credits illustration assistance.

P1.justification: V4 makes limited prose and caption edits, updates cross-references, changes correspondence-footnote formatting, and adds an acknowledgment. Section organization remains stable. The conclusion introduces the dangling phrase 'near its maximum likelihood parameters.'

P2.justification: V4 substantially reorganizes the main visual presentation: it adds the sampling-to-detection illustration in Figure 2, redraws Figure 1, moves the original histogram to Figure 3 near the case study, and stacks the sample-count panels beside a reformatted Table 5. Table 2 and Algorithm 1 also move; their content is retained.

improvement.justification: The new Figure 2 makes the connection between model perturbation, temperature sampling, answer aggregation, and detection easier to follow. This provides a modest explanatory gain while preserving the scientific evidence. More compressed sample-count plots and the new sentence fragment in Section 6 slightly detract from presentation quality.
